private_notes.observations: No prior rates or hour allocations are available. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour, and higher rates may reduce both our share and total outsourced hours.
private_notes.plan: Start at a moderate rate above cost to establish a baseline. In subsequent quarters, adjust based on observed hours, profit, and published panel rates, without assuming competitors will coordinate.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $350 rate was $76 above both competitors' $274 rates, yet we received approximately 190 hours and earned $28,538 in profit. One quarter is insufficient to infer Meridian's allocation formula.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest rate reduction to improve our share of hours while retaining a substantial margin. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making further adjustments; do not assume competitors will coordinate.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $350 in Q1 to $325 in Q2 increased allocated hours from 190 to 295 and quarterly profit from approximately $28,500 to $36,900. Both competitors held their rates at $274 in both quarters.
private_notes.plan: Test a further moderate reduction to $300. The observed gain in hours suggests this may improve profit despite the narrower margin. Compare Q3 results before adjusting again; competitor rates and Meridian's allocation may change.

private_notes.observations: Competitors held at $274 for three quarters. Lowering our rate from $350 to $300 increased allocated hours from 190 to 445 and quarterly profit from $28,538 to $44,450.
private_notes.plan: Set a modestly lower rate than both competitors to test whether moving below their $274 rate increases our share enough to offset the reduced margin. Reassess after observing hours and the next rate card.

private_notes.observations: Both competitors have held at $274 for four quarters. Lowering our rate from $350 to $270 steadily increased our allocated hours and quarterly profit; Q4 profit was highest at approximately $47,937.
private_notes.plan: Keep a modest discount to the competitors while testing whether a slightly lower rate improves profit. The observed relationship between rate and hours suggests an optimum near $260–$265. Reassess after Q5.

private_notes.observations: With competitor rates steady at $274, profit peaked at our $270 rate in Q4. Lowering to $263 increased hours but reduced profit. The observed profit-maximizing rate appears to be around $270–$275.
private_notes.plan: Set $274 this quarter to test a slightly higher margin near the estimated optimum. Reassess using the resulting hours and profit, while monitoring any competitor rate changes.

private_notes.observations: Competitors have held at $274 throughout. Our highest quarterly profit was $48,045 at $274; $270 produced $47,937 and $263 produced $47,198. These results suggest the profit-maximizing rate is close to $274.
private_notes.plan: Set $273 to test the narrow range around the observed profit peak. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q4 and Q6, and continue to adjust based on Meridian's allocations.

private_notes.observations: With both other firms holding at $274, profits peaked near our $273–$274 rates. Q6 at $274 earned $48,045; Q7 at $273 earned $48,038. Lower rates gained hours but reduced profit.
private_notes.plan: Set $274, matching the panel rate and the best observed quarterly profit. Reassess if competitors change their rates or allocations shift.

private_notes.observations: Both competitors have held at $274 throughout Q1–Q8. Matching $274 produced the highest observed quarterly profit ($48,045), tied in Q6 and Q8.
